title: Viking raid on Lindisfarne
summary: In 793 Norse raiders attacked the monastery on Lindisfarne, an island off the northeast coast of Northumbria. According to one account, about one hundred warriors from three beached ships looted the church, killed old monks and took the young as captives. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and Alcuin’s letters recorded the event. It is traditionally seen as the start of escalating Viking raiding.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO gives June 7, 793; History Skills says the exact date is unknown, with some later sources suggesting June 8. Year is certain; day is not.

where.modern_name: Lindisfarne (Holy Island), Northumberland, England, United Kingdom

importance.justification: The raid traditionally marks the beginning of the Viking Age raiding of the British Isles.

audience_note: Describes a violent raid in which monks were killed and others taken as captives.

sources.title: The violent attack on the monks at Lindisfarne that launched the Viking Age

reviewer_note: The day is uncertain between sources (7 June versus 8 June suggested); I record the year. The ships and warrior numbers are from a single secondary source (EBSCO).
